models_evaluated: PAICS (Prenatal Ultrasound Diagnosis Artificial Intelligence Conduct System)

links.outcome: Sonographer sensitivity and specificity for fetal intracranial malformations with vs without AI assistance in a randomised crossover trial
links.effect: Fetal-based sensitivity increased by 0·087 (95% CI 0·029 to 0·147; p superiority<0·0001); specificity non-inferior (difference 0·009, 95% CI -0·006 to 0·023). No AI-related adverse events reported.
links.quote: In the fetal-based analysis, sensitivity increased by 0·087 (95% CI 0·029 to 0·147; p<sub>superiority</sub><0·0001), with specificity meeting the non-inferiority criterion (difference 0·009, 95% CI -0·006 to 0·023; p<sub>non-inferiority</sub><0·0001).

links.outcome: Human-AI team performance compared with sonographers without AI in intended deployment mode
links.effect: Malformation-targeted sensitivity improved by 0·118 (95% CI 0·054 to 0·181; p superiority<0·0001); specificity non-inferior (difference 0·001, 95% CI -0·001 to 0·002).
links.quote: In the malformation-targeted analysis, sensitivity improved by 0·118 (95% CI 0·054 to 0·181; p<sub>superiority</sub><0·0001), and specificity was also non-inferior (difference 0·001, 95% CI -0·001 to 0·002; p<sub>non-inferiority</sub><0·0001).

screen.reason: Multicentre randomized controlled trial evaluating the impact of AI assistance on sonographer diagnostic performance during prenatal ultrasound scanning in real-world clinical practice.
